### Added
- **`tests/verify-bom-charts.py`, wired into `make verify-meta`: every chart the BOM pins is rendered against the values the meta chart forwards to it** (giantswarm/agent-platform#278). `verify-meta` rendered the meta chart alone — it proved the HelmReleases and their values were shaped as intended, never that the chart on the other end accepts them, so a key forwarded unconditionally against a pin whose schema forbids it was invisible until an installation failed to reconcile. The check pulls each pinned chart at the version and from the registry its rendered `OCIRepository` names (so the ghcr.io components — kagent, Substrate — and cloudnative-pg are covered, not just the gsoci ones) and renders it with exactly the values its release carries, failing only on a schema rejection: a later template error means the values were accepted and the chart wanted an input the BOM alone does not carry, which is reported apart and counted apart. Every BOM-pinned component is enabled for the render, so a pin cannot drop out of the check because the golden render leaves that component off, and a pin with no `OCIRepository` or one resolved to another version fails rather than skipping silently — 21 of 21 pins covered. A self-test proves against the installed Helm that a schema rejection and a template failure are still told apart, so a reworded Helm message fails the check loudly instead of downgrading the break it exists for into a passing line. Deliberately stdlib-only, like `tests/verify-toolset-presets.py`: the CI image has no PyYAML. It found the two pins above on unmodified `main` on its first run.
### Fixed
- **The actors' egress opens the host model servers model-manager fronts** (giantswarm/agent-platform#278). `model-manager` with a host backend (`ollama`, `lemonade`, `lmstudio`) wires every pulled model into kagent as a `ModelConfig` pointing at that server — but only model-manager's own policy opened it, and an actor's inference request leaves through Agent Substrate's egress gateway (`substrate-atenet-egress`), whose allow-list carries muster, the kagent controller, the tool server and `world:443`. A host model server is on neither 443 nor HTTPS, so every such request was dropped while model-manager reported the model as wired and healthy. The egress gateway now opens each host backend at the address the ModelConfigs actually carry — `model-manager.<backend>.agentHost`, falling back to `.endpoint` — as a `toCIDR` for an IP and a `toFQDNs` plus `cluster` arm for a hostname, and renders nothing while model-manager is off, for a `kserve`-only backend list or in the kubernetes flavour. A hostname arm also switches that policy's DNS rule to `agent-platform.dnsEgressWithProxy`: Cilium fills its FQDN cache only from answers its own proxy sees, so without it the `toFQDNs` selector never matches and the name stays blocked; an IP-only backend list keeps the plain rule, so no installation gains an L7 DNS proxy on every actor lookup it did not need. `model-manager.<backend>.agentHost` is now guarded like `.endpoint` — an `http(s)` URL with a host — because the policies parse it with `urlParse`, which answered an empty `matchName` with port 80 for a scheme-less value and died on a raw parse error for a `host:port` one. `make verify-kagent-netpol` covers all of it.
- **The customer BOM pins two charts that reject the values the meta chart forwards to them** (giantswarm/agent-platform#278, found by the check below). `gateway.parameters.podAnnotations` and `klausGateway.podDisruptionBudget` / `.podAnnotations` travel unconditionally since #431, and `vm-manager` / `vmManager` since #441, while the BOM pinned `agent-platform-connectivity` 4.8.0 and `klaus-gateway` 1.0.2 — both `additionalProperties: false`, so a BOM-pinned installation got two releases that could not install or upgrade whatever the operator set (`additional properties 'podAnnotations' not allowed`; `additional properties 'vmManager', 'vm-manager' not allowed`). Checked release by release: connectivity is rejected through 4.10.0 on the #431 keys and through 4.10.6 on the #441 ones, and accepted from **4.11.0**; klaus-gateway is rejected at 1.0.3 and accepted from **1.1.0** — the release the #431 entry already names for its budget knob. **A BOM-pinned installation should take these pins.**
